feedback: Written before this robot has raced. Iteration 0 (±2 outer weights, kp 3, y=0.05) gave one line loss per run and max_error 0.062 to 0.065 m on every track, so the steering gain was roughly right in size but the sensing was too short. Iteration 1 (±1.0 outer weights, kp 4, y=0.06) cut oval progress from 0.53 to 0.36 and still lost the line on the s-bend (0.55) and slalom (0.25), so the lower weight scale under-steers. Iteration 2 (±1.0 weights, kp 6, y=0.08) was the best result at 190.17. Its oval progress was 0.70 and slalom losses fell to 0, but the s-bend still lost the line once per run at max_error 0.0626. Your geometry is held at iteration 2's values, so the next race isolates steering authority. The Integrator is raising the outer weights to ±1.5 and kp to 5.0 with kd 0.8. Decide the next geometry change from the next race: if line_loss_events on the s-bend is still at least 1 with max_error near 0.06 m, the limit is turn rate per unit of steering command, not sensor reach. If steering_oscillation rises sharply while max_error stays below 0.06 m, the gain is too high for the current damping, so back off the authority rather than changing the sensors.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events stays at 1 or more on the s-bend with max_error near 0.06 m, reduce wheel_track from 0.12 to 0.10 m. Turn rate is the wheel speed difference divided by wheel_track, so a narrower track gives more yaw per steering command. This follows from iteration 2's s-bend loss at a steering authority the controller could not reach.

If the line is still lost at the tight bend but the sensors read near-zero on the outer pair, increase sensor_size from 0.012 to 0.016 with the same spread. A larger footprint keeps more tape in view at the edge, which reduces the chance that all sensors fall below the 0.05 line-loss threshold, as the slalom and s-bend losses in iterations 1 and 2 suggest.

If steering_oscillation rises sharply on the oval with max_error below 0.06 m, keep the geometry at iteration 2's values and do not change the body. Iteration 0 showed that high gain overshoots, and body_width cannot help because the off-track limit stays at the 0.06 m floor for every allowed body width.
